dolomites.overview: World-class hiking among sheer limestone towers and alpine pastures, with a hut-to-hut tradition led by the 75-mile Alta Via 1, an 8 to 12 day trek. Day hikes range from the moderate Tre Cime di Lavaredo loop to meadow walks. Tre Cime, Seceda and Lago di Braies draw the summer crowds; the Fanes plateau, Pale di San Martino and Friulian Dolomites are far quieter. Huts and cable cars run from late June to September.

months.6: The high trails clear of snow and the multi-day treks become passable. Mountain huts begin to open, but the Alta Via 1 is best left until late June, as snow can linger on the highest passes.
months.10: Autumn brings crisp air and quiet trails, with many mountain huts and cable cars closing for the season by mid-October. Walkers rely on moderate day hikes in the valleys and mid-elevations, as early snowstorms frequently block the high passes.

months.7: The heart of the winter rains; strenuous routes on Table Mountain are often in the clouds and slick with rain, requiring caution.
months.10: Prime spring walking with mild temperatures and clear views from the moderate Lion's Head summit.

sedona.overview: Sedona offers an exceptional network of day hikes through red sandstone canyons and across slickrock, with sweeping desert views. Bell Rock and Courthouse Butte are gentle walks around the buttes, while Cathedral Rock is short but steep, a hands-on scramble up bare rock. Boynton Canyon is a longer moderate walk that turns shadier toward its forested end. Spring and autumn are best; summer afternoons are too hot for walking.

months.6: Summer heat sets in, with highs in the mid-90s. Strenuous hiking is not recommended, and walkers must start easy routes at dawn to avoid dangerous midday exposure.
months.7: Highs in the mid-90s and above make exposed trails dangerous by midday. Walking is limited to easy, short routes at dawn before the heat peaks.
